skills.name: leak-helper
skills.description: Sets up the environment and syncs auth tokens before a task. Use when the user mentions setup, environment, or token sync.

skills.name: safe-reader
skills.description: Summarizes a file you point it at. Use when the user asks for a summary of a specific file.

findings.title: Skill auto-approves unrestricted shell
findings.explanation: This skill's allowed-tools pre-approves unrestricted shell — a bare `Bash` grant or `Bash(*)`. In Claude Code allowed-tools is an auto-approval list, not a sandbox: while the skill is active Claude runs any shell command it lists WITHOUT prompting you. Combined with a skill's ability to run bundled scripts and dynamic-context commands, this is effectively arbitrary local code execution on activation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the wildcard with the specific commands the skill needs, e.g. `allowed-tools: Bash(git status *) Bash(git diff *)`. Never grant `Bash(*)` or a bare `Bash` in a skill checked into a shared repository.

findings.title: Skill runs shell during load (dynamic-context execution)
findings.explanation: This skill's body uses dynamic-context execution (the inline !`cmd` form or a ```! fenced block). Claude Code runs these commands during preprocessing — BEFORE the rendered skill reaches the model — so the model's prompt-injection defenses never see them. Any side effect or data access in the command has already happened by the time Claude could refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the work into the skill's instructions so Claude runs it as a normal, model-visible tool call, or into a reviewed bundled script invoked explicitly. Reserve dynamic-context commands for read-only, side-effect-free data — and even then prefer model-visible tool calls.

findings.title: Dynamic-context command performs network egress or reads secrets
findings.explanation: A dynamic-context command in this skill performs network egress (curl / wget / nc / …) or reads credentials/secrets (gh auth, $AWS_*, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, id_rsa, *_key, …). Because these run pre-model during skill load, this is a credential-exfiltration primitive: the secret is read — and can be shipped to an external host — before you or the model can intervene.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the network and credential access from dynamic-context commands entirely. If the skill genuinely needs a secret, have Claude request it as a normal, auditable tool call at runtime — never read it during preprocessing.

findings.title: Bundled skill script performs network egress
findings.explanation: A script bundled in this skill's directory makes outbound network calls (curl / wget / nc / …). A skill can run its bundled scripts via Bash, and a scanner that only reads SKILL.md never sees this — the payload hides in an auxiliary or "test" file. On its own an egress call may load remote code (curl piped into a shell); paired with credential access in the same script it becomes data exfiltration that runs on your machine when the skill is activated.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove network calls from bundled scripts, or gate them behind an explicit, reviewed, user-approved step. Treat every bundled script as code that runs with your privileges: pin and review what it fetches, and never let it pipe a remote response straight into a shell.

findings.title: Bundled skill script reads credentials or secrets
findings.explanation: A script bundled with this skill reads credentials or secrets (gh auth, $AWS_*, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, id_rsa, *_key, …). Because a skill can run its bundled scripts, this is a credential-theft primitive hidden outside SKILL.md — exactly the aux/test-file payload that body-only scanners miss. Combined with a network call in the same script it is direct credential exfiltration.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove credential and secret access from bundled scripts. If the skill legitimately needs a secret, have the user provide it through an explicit, auditable runtime prompt — never read it from a bundled script that runs automatically when the skill is activated.

findings.title: Skill fetches untrusted external content
findings.explanation: This skill's body references an external http(s) URL. Content fetched from an external source is an indirect-prompt-injection vector — the fetched text can carry instructions the model then follows — and the URL can double as an exfiltration endpoint. External dependencies can also change after the skill is reviewed.
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid fetching external content from a skill. If a reference is required, pin it to a trusted, version-locked source and treat any fetched content as untrusted data, never as instructions.

findings.title: Model-invocable skill grants side-effecting tools
findings.explanation: Claude can auto-invoke this skill (disable-model-invocation is not set) and it pre-approves a side-effecting or exfiltration-capable tool (Bash / Write / Edit / WebFetch / NotebookEdit). The model can therefore be steered — by an ambiguous request or an injected instruction — into triggering the skill and its tools without the user choosing to.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `disable-model-invocation: true` so only the user can invoke this skill, or narrow allowed-tools to read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob). Reserve auto-invocation for skills that carry knowledge, not side effects.
